meta.topic: EU instant payments maximum amount regulatory change

problem:
Aldergrove Manufacturing, a corporate customer of Meridian Bank, wants to pay a supplier 250,000 euro instantly on a Friday afternoon. The payments team at the bank is unsure whether the payment can go as an instant payment at all. An older internal guide still says the scheme maximum for instant euro payments is 100,000 euro, and the product configuration enforces that cap. A newer colleague says the cap has been removed, and the customer is pressing for an answer before the supplier's deadline. Meanwhile the bank's own product limit for instant payments is 50,000 euro for this customer segment, and the fraud team has a separate velocity limit on large instant payments. Three different numbers are in play, and nobody in the room can say with confidence which one governs.

The facts that settle the question come from the current scheme and regulatory position. The EPC SCT Inst Rulebook 2025 removed the 100,000 euro scheme maximum, effective 5 October 2025, so there is now no scheme-level maximum for instant euro payments. Regulation (EU) 2024/886 requires a maximum execution time of 10 seconds, with sub-timelines of 5, 7 and 9 seconds for the stages within that window. Verification of Payee is mandatory for instant euro payments from 9 October 2025. None of that removes the bank's own right to set a lower product limit or a customer-level risk limit, but those limits must be presented as the bank's own, not as a scheme cap.

The bank must separate the four layers, scheme maximum, regulatory obligation, bank product limit and customer-level risk limit, decide their precedence, set an effective date for the change, and update routing, channels, customer terms and communications consistently. A payment above the bank's product limit but below any scheme maximum must be handled by the bank's own rule, for example by routing it to a non-instant rail or by seeking an approved exception, and the customer must be told which limit applied and why.
solution:
First, establish the authoritative facts and record them with their sources and effective dates. The scheme maximum of 100,000 euro was removed by the EPC SCT Inst Rulebook 2025, effective 5 October 2025, and there is now no scheme-level maximum. The regulatory execution obligation is a maximum of 10 seconds under Regulation (EU) 2024/886, and Verification of Payee is mandatory for instant euro payments from 9 October 2025. The old 100,000 euro figure must be removed from every guide, configuration comment and training slide, because a stale number in one place will be quoted as the rule.

Second, define the limit hierarchy explicitly and implement it as effective-dated configuration. The order is: regulatory obligations first, then the scheme rules, then the bank's product limit, then the customer-level risk limit, with the strictest applicable limit winning for any given payment. For Aldergrove Manufacturing, that means the 50,000 euro product limit governs the 250,000 euro request, and the correct handling is to route it to the appropriate non-instant rail or to an approved exception process, with the customer told plainly that the bank's product limit applied, not a scheme cap.

Third, manage the transition. Apply the new scheme position from its effective date, decide how in-flight and standing instructions are treated, update every channel consistently so the mobile app, the corporate portal and the API give the same answer, and update customer terms and communications. Regression-test the hierarchy with cases above and below each limit, including a payment above the customer limit but below the old scheme maximum, and keep a rule inventory that records which rulebook version and regulation applies to each payment date.

decision.question: You are the business analyst for Meridian Bank. A corporate customer wants to send 250,000 euro instantly. The old internal guide says the scheme maximum is 100,000 euro. The current rulebook has removed that scheme maximum, but the bank's own product limit for this customer is 50,000 euro. The customer asks which limit applies.

options.label: A
options.detail: Reject the payment, citing the old 100,000 euro scheme maximum.

options.label: B
options.detail: Apply the limit hierarchy: no scheme maximum now applies, but the bank's stricter product and customer risk limits govern, so route the payment to the appropriate non-instant rail or an approved exception process and explain which limit applied.

options.label: C
options.detail: Send it instantly, ignoring the bank's product limit because the scheme cap is gone.

options.label: D
options.detail: Split the payment into five instant payments of 50,000 euro to work around the product limit.

decisionRationale: Option B is correct because it separates the layers: the scheme maximum no longer exists, but the bank's own product and risk limits still govern and must be enforced transparently. Option A teaches an outdated rule, since the 100,000 euro scheme maximum was removed effective 5 October 2025. Option C ignores the bank's legitimate risk controls. Option D is structuring to evade a limit and creates reconciliation and fraud risks.

steps.title: Submits a 250,000 euro instant payment instruction through the corporate portal
Evaluates the payment against the scheme rules, the bank product limit and the customer risk limit in precedence order
Checks the beneficiary name against the account before the payment proceeds
Routes the payment: instant if within all limits, otherwise to the non-instant rail or the exception process
Executes the instant payment within the 10-second maximum where the instant route applies
Settles the instant payment and returns confirmation
Tells the customer the outcome and, where a limit applied, which limit and why
Posts the debit and credit and updates the customer balance

happy: A payment within the scheme rules and within the bank's product and customer limits is verified, executed within 10 seconds, confirmed to the customer, and settled. A payment above the bank's product limit is routed to the appropriate non-instant rail or exception process, and the customer is told clearly that the bank's product limit applied, not a scheme cap.

negative.title: Conflicting limits
negative.detail: A payment is above the customer limit but below the old scheme maximum, and different channels give different answers. Apply the single governed hierarchy in the limits service for every channel, so all channels enforce the same strictest applicable limit and give the same explanation.

negative.title: Effective-date transition
negative.detail: A payment is processed around the date the scheme maximum was removed and the old rule is still in configuration. Use effective-dated rules keyed to the payment date, remove the stale 100,000 euro figure from all configuration, and regression-test payments dated before and after the change.

negative.title: Verification of Payee mismatch
negative.detail: The beneficiary name does not match the account for a large instant payment. Warn the customer with the Verification of Payee result, do not proceed without the customer's informed decision, and record the outcome and the customer's choice.

negative.title: Instant execution exceeds 10 seconds
negative.detail: A dependency is slow and the payment cannot complete within the regulatory maximum. Apply the timeout and confirmation rules, do not leave the payment in an unknown state, and report the outcome to the customer with the defined next steps.

technical: Implement limits as effective-dated configuration in a single limits service, with separate fields for scheme maximum, regulatory obligation, bank product limit and customer risk limit, each with its owner, source and effective dates. Never hard-code the old 100,000 euro figure anywhere. Record the rule version applied to each payment, including the rulebook version and the regulation, so a payment can be reconstructed later. Use correlation IDs across the limits check, Verification of Payee, execution and confirmation. Apply the 10-second execution budget as a measured service level with sub-timeline monitoring at 5, 7 and 9 seconds, and alert when the budget is at risk. Keep the routing decision, the limit that governed it and the customer explanation in the audit record.

accounting: An instant payment that executes creates an immediate debit and settlement entry, so Treasury must hold liquidity for large instant outflows even though there is no longer a scheme maximum to cap them. Payments routed to a non-instant rail instead follow that rail's value date and settlement timing, and the customer statement must show the rail actually used. Operations monitors instant execution times against the 10-second maximum and investigates breaches, and the limits service changes are subject to a governed release with customer communications for any product-limit change. A payment that exceeds the execution window must be reconciled as an exception, never left in an unknown state.
